claims.text: Oxidation resistance in MPEAs is governed primarily by formation of a continuous, coherent oxide scale.
The protective oxide scale is enriched in Cr, Al, and Si, which are described as refractory elements.
A continuous, coherent oxide scale acts as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
Restricting oxygen diffusion limits further oxidation.
Restricting oxygen diffusion limits deleterious phase transformations that compromise material integrity.
The proposed baseline MPEA has a heterogeneous microstructure and moderate refractory-element content.
The proposed baseline MPEA tends to form nonuniform or discontinuous oxide layers during high-temperature oxidation.
A controlled comparison should use a baseline MPEA and a compositionally modified MPEA with increased refractory-element content, processed using identical thermomechanical treatments.
The two alloy sets should be exposed under identical sustained oxidizing conditions around 1000 degrees Celsius in air or an oxygen-rich atmosphere.
Increasing refractory-element concentration promotes selective oxidation.
Selective oxidation induced by refractory-element enrichment produces a more uniform and adherent protective scale.
The refractory-element-enriched protective scale grows more slowly than the baseline scale.
The enriched protective scale reduces oxygen ingress into the underlying alloy matrix.
Reduced oxygen ingress preserves the underlying microstructure and prevents rapid degradation.
The modified alloy will form a thinner oxide scale than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will form a more uniform and chemically stable oxide scale than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will show a lower oxidation rate, indicated by lower mass gain, than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will show shallower oxygen penetration and fewer microstructural defects than the baseline alloy.
The proposed behavior is expected only where thermal shock, cyclic loading, or other mechanical stresses do not introduce additional failure modes.
The beneficial effect may diminish at temperatures or exposure times beyond the stability regime of the protective scale.
